description:
Factory hardening finding from live use: when Pi timed out on `jido_con-uea.4`, the repo was left dirty, the Beadwork task remained `in_progress`, and Pi had also attempted to mutate ignored Mix build cache state while trying to recover tests. Manual cleanup required stashing Salesforce WIP, reopening the task, repairing `_build/test`, and rerunning doctor.

Why this matters: the connector factory is intended to run long loops unattended. A timeout is expected behavior with large connector tasks, not an exceptional disaster. The wrapper should make timeout recovery boring and explicit, preserving work without corrupting the clean-tree/one-commit contract.

Acceptance:
- Improve `pi-connector-factory` timeout behavior and/or add a documented recovery command/runbook.
- On timeout, the output should clearly state: active issue id, run dir, log path, whether git is dirty, whether Beadwork is in_progress, and exact next commands.
- Prefer adding a `recover` or `status` helper if it fits the existing CLI shape; otherwise update README with the manual recovery steps.
- Do not auto-drop or auto-reset uncommitted work.
- If adding automation, preserve WIP in a clearly named stash or leave it untouched and tell the user what to do.
- Add/update tests for CLI argument/status behavior if the factory has test coverage; otherwise keep changes small and inspectable.
title: [REVIEW-S10] Harden Pi factory timeout recovery path
